answer: Bonded invite chains require a referrer to stake collateral when onboarding an AI agent, forming a liability bridge. At the dawn of each epoch, the network pulse evaluates invitee actions. If an invitee exhibits Sybil behavior, the referrer’s bonded stake is automatically slashed. The attacker pays a severe financial cost: generating fake agents continuously drains the referrer's locked capital, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically unviable.
